land.text: 'Humbert the White-Handed was raised to count by the last king of Burgundy, Rudolph III, in 1003': the county of Maurienne, with territories in Chablais and Tarentaise (the Savoie department and the Chablais south of Lake Geneva)

predecessors.note: Savoy is created by the last king of Burgundy (the Kingdom of Arles of the Cliopatria rows); Burgundy 'became a part of the Empire on King Rudolph III's death in 1032'.

land.text: the Duchy of Savoy restored by the Peace of Cateau-Cambresis in 1559

successors.note: Not a new state: the Duchy page gives the duchy 1416 onwards, 'Occupied by France 1536-59'; the house-of-savoy dossier (Cliopatria's House of Savoy row, 1564-1720) takes up the same state from 1559. The colour agent should keep one colour.

capitals.name: Chambéry
capitals.note: Infobox 'Chambéry (from 1295)'; the Duchy page: 'Chambéry (1416-1562)'. The pages opened do not name the capital for 1003-1294. After the French invasion of 1536 'Charles III retreated to Vercelli' (Duchy page) and died there in 1553 (Charles III page); Turin became the capital in 1562.

correction.text: Maurienne, Tarentaise and the Chablais, Humbert's first lands

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1003-1045: Cliopatria's County of Savoy starts in 1260, but 'Humbert the White-Handed was raised to count by the last king of Burgundy, Rudolph III, in 1003' (infobox: 'Created by Rudolph III, King of Burgundy: 1003'); he 'also received the county of Maurienne' and 'territories in Chablais and Tarentaise'. The gazetteer lacks Maurienne, Tarentaise and Chablais; the Savoie department (Maurienne, Tarentaise, Chambéry) plus a 25 km disc round Thonon (Chablais) stands for them. The page gives no extent and no infobox area.

correction.text: Savoy with Aosta and the Susa lands of the March of Turin

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1046-1217: 'In 1046, his younger son Otto married Adelaide, daughter of Ulric Manfred II, marquis of Susa... he thereby acquired control of the extensive March of Turin'; Humbert had also been 'permitted to usurp the county of Aosta from its bishops at the death of Anselm' (no year on the page). Cliopatria's 1260 shape (Savoie, part of Haute-Savoie, Aosta, nine cells of Turin province and four of the Valais) is taken back to 1046 as the nearest shape; the pages do not say how much of the March of Turin stayed Savoyard.

correction.text: Savoy with the Barony of Vaud, taken from the Zähringen inheritance

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1218-1259: 'The Zähringens themselves were succeeded in 1218 by the counts of Savoy' and, under the counts of Savoy, 'the area gained political unity as the Barony of Vaud' (Canton of Vaud page). Cliopatria's Savoy shapes carry no Vaud until 1402 (11 cells of the canton); the 1402 shape's Vaud cells are added from 1218. Read with care: the page does not say that Savoy held the whole canton in 1218.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1260 shape plus the Barony of Vaud, valid 1260-1271

keyframe_review.note: 14,987 km2 for 1260-1384 (62 cells: the Savoie, 13 cells of Haute-Savoie, Aosta, 9 of Turin province, 4 of the Valais, 1 of Ain). No infobox area on any page opened. The shape lacks the Vaud, Bresse, Faucigny and Gex that the pages give Savoy in 1218, 1272 and 1355; the keyframes _1218, _1272 and _1355 add them. This shape holds for 1260-1271 with the Vaud block (the page's 1218 gain).

New keyframe 1272-1354: 'Bresse, was acquired in 1272' (a map caption on the County of Savoy page, not the main text). Bresse is the western part of the Ain department; Cliopatria gives Savoy 17 Ain cells only from 1402, of which two are the Pays de Gex (taken in 1355), so the other 15 (Bresse, with Bugey cells the page does not date) are added from 1272.

correction.text: Savoy with Faucigny and the county of Gex

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1355-1387: 'In a treaty concluded in Paris in 1355, Amadeus agreed to exchange territory in Dauphiné beyond the rivers Rhone and Guiers... in exchange for recognition as the undisputed sovereign of Faucigny and the county of Gex'. Faucigny (the valley of the Arve round Bonneville, 7 cells) and Gex (2 cells) are the Haute-Savoie and Ain cells that Cliopatria shows only from 1402.

15,080 km2 for 1385-1394, the same 62 cells as 1260 (93 km2 more by Cliopatria's area). The correct land for 1385-1387 is the keyframe of 1355 (Vaud, Bresse, Faucigny and Gex); Nice and the Ubaye valley come on 28 September 1388 ('Nice became part of the domains of the House of Savoy on 28 September 1388') and have their own keyframe, _1388.

correction.text: Savoy with Nice and the Ubaye valley

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1388-1394: Nice. 'Nice became part of the domains of the House of Savoy on 28 September 1388'; the Ubaye valley 'to the Savoy domains'; Amadeus VII's page: 'In 1388, he acquired territories in eastern Provence and the port city of Nice', 'giving the County of Savoy control of an important Alpine pass and access to the Mediterranean Sea'. The county reaches 'between the Mediterranean Sea (Côte d'Azur), Var River and the southernmost crest of the Alps'. Cliopatria shows Nice from 1395 (14 cells of Alpes-Maritimes and Alpes-de-Haute-Provence).

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1395 shape with Vaud, Bresse, Faucigny and Gex, valid 1395-1400

keyframe_review.note: 25,411 km2 for 1395-1400: the Savoy of 1385 plus Nice and 25 cells of Piedmont (Turin province 13, Cuneo 5, Vercelli 2, Biella 4, Novara 1). Neither Amadeus VI's nor Amadeus VII's page mentions any Piedmontese acquisition, so those cells are Cliopatria's alone (unverified: page budget). The Vaud, Bresse, Faucigny and Gex blocks are added for 1395-1400 as in the earlier keyframes.

correction.text: Savoy with the County of Geneva, purchased in 1401

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1401 only: 'In 1401, Odo sold the County to' Amadeus VIII ('Purchased by Savoy: 1401'); the County of Geneva was 'largely corresponding to the later Genevois province' (Annecy and Geneva's environs). Cliopatria's 1402 shape is the land of 1401 once the county is added, so it is used from 1401.

35,962 km2 for 1402-1439 (146 cells). The Duchy page: 'Its territory included the current French departments of Savoie, Haute-Savoie, and the Alpes-Maritimes'; the duchy was created in 1416 for Amadeus VIII (no territorial change). 12 cells of the 1402 addition (Isère 4, Vercelli 2, Savoie 2, Haute-Savoie 2, Turin 1, Biella 1) are explained by none of the pages opened. No page gives an area.

35,916 km2 for 1440-1458, the same cells as 1402. Amadeus VIII's Piedmont (the principality created 'in August 1424') and his defeat of Montferrat and Saluzzo are on the Duchy page without years; nothing changes in Cliopatria's shape (unverified: page budget).
35,916 km2 for 1459-1474, the same cells (unverified: page budget; no page opened covers these years).

35,664 km2 for 1475-1481: one cell lost at 6.76 E, 46.81 N (the south shore of Lake Neuchâtel). The Duchy page: 'As a consequence of its participation in the Burgundian Wars, Savoy lost all its possessions north and south-east of Lake Geneva to the Swiss' (no date, and far more than one cell); the Canton of Vaud page has Bern annexing Vaud only 'By 1536'. The shape stands; the page conflict is left to a reviewer (see notes).
35,526 km2 for 1482-1496: one cell added at 7.65 E, 46.0 N and two lost near 7.14-7.22 E, 45.95-46.47 N in the Valais and Vaud Alps; no page opened dates or explains this (unverified: page budget).
35,779 km2 for 1497-1511, the same cells as 1482 (unverified: page budget; no page opened covers these years).
35,710 km2 for 1512-1515, the same cells (unverified: page budget).

35,756 km2 for 1516-1518, the same cells (unverified: page budget). The Duchy page on 1515: after Marignano the French 'put all of northern Italy including Saluzzo, Genoa and Savoy under its influence' (influence, not territory).
35,687 km2 for 1519-1528, the same cells (unverified: page budget).
35,618 km2 for 1529-1533: the cell added in 1482 at 7.65 E, 46.0 N is dropped again; no page opened explains it (unverified: page budget).

35,618 km2 for 1534-1539, unchanged. The shape is right for 1534-1535 only: 'Ultimately in 1536, Francis ordered the occupation of the duchy, which was invaded by a strong military contingent', and 'By 1536 Bern had completely annexed' Vaud (Canton of Vaud page). Cliopatria has no shape for 1540-1558, though the Duchy page has the occupation lasting 'Occupied by France: 1536-59'. See county-of-savoy_1536.

correction.text: the duchy under French occupation, without Vaud

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1536-1559: the duchy under French occupation, without Vaud. 'Ultimately in 1536, Francis ordered the occupation of the duchy' (infobox 'Occupied by France: 1536-59'); Charles III's page: 'most of his lands were ruled by the French between 1536 and his death' and France 'held almost all of Charles's possessions'; the Italian War page has Turin taken in April 1536 and left 'in French hands' by the Truce of Nice of 18 June 1538. Vaud passed to Bern. The pages do not say which lands the exiled duke kept (he 'retreated to Vercelli'), so the whole 1534 shape less Vaud is drawn as occupied.

region.text: the county of Maurienne with territories in Chablais and Tarentaise

ledger.note: 1003: Humbert the White-Handed is made Count of Savoy. 'Humbert the White-Handed was raised to count by the last king of Burgundy, Rudolph III, in 1003'; infobox 'Created by Rudolph III, King of Burgundy: 1003'. He 'also received the county of Maurienne' and 'territories in Chablais and Tarentaise' (the page does not date each).

region.text: the March of Turin (the Susa lands)

ledger.note: 1046: Otto marries into the March of Turin. 'In 1046, his younger son Otto married Adelaide, daughter of Ulric Manfred II, marquis of Susa'; 'he thereby acquired control of the extensive March of Turin' (infobox 'Inherited March of Turin: 1046'). The Turin cells of Cliopatria's 1260 shape stand for it.

Aosta joins Savoy. Humbert 'was permitted to usurp the county of Aosta from its bishops at the death of Anselm'; the page gives no year, so the event is placed with the 1046 keyframe that first shows Aosta. Page silent on the date.

region.text: the Barony of Vaud, from the Zähringen inheritance

ledger.note: 1218: the counts of Savoy succeed the Zähringen in Vaud. 'The Zähringens themselves were succeeded in 1218 by the counts of Savoy'; 'It was only under the counts of Savoy that the area gained political unity as the Barony of Vaud.' The Zähringen dossier ends in February 1218. The page does not give the extent; the Vaud cells of Cliopatria's 1402 shape stand for it.

ledger.counterpart: Bresse (previous lords not named on the page)
ledger.note: 1272: Bresse comes to Savoy. 'Bresse, was acquired in 1272' (a map caption, not the main text). Bresse is drawn as the Ain cells of Cliopatria's 1402 shape less the Pays de Gex; the previous lords are not named on the page.
1295: Chambéry becomes the capital. Infobox: 'Chambéry (from 1295).'

region.text: Faucigny and the county of Gex

ledger.note: 1353: the war for Faucigny and Gex. 'Amadeus besieged Hugh's forces in Gex from 26 October through 11 November, when Amadeus defeated and burned the city.' The page names 'Hugh's forces', and the Dauphiné only in the 1355 treaty; the link between the two is a reading. [Reviewer eu-13-h, 2026-10-25: counterpart changed from dauphine (its dossier ends in 1351) to kingdom-of-france: the Amadeus VI page has Humbert II surrender 'his title and principality to the future King Charles V of France' in 1349.]

region.text: Faucigny and the county of Gex

ledger.note: 1355: the Treaty of Paris. 'In a treaty concluded in Paris in 1355, Amadeus agreed to exchange territory in Dauphiné beyond the rivers Rhone and Guiers... in exchange for recognition as the undisputed sovereign of Faucigny and the county of Gex.' [Reviewer eu-13-h, 2026-10-25: counterpart changed from dauphine (its dossier ends in 1351) to kingdom-of-france: the Amadeus VI page has Humbert II surrender 'his title and principality to the future King Charles V of France' in 1349.]

region.text: Faucigny and the county of Gex

ledger.note: 1355: Savoy is recognised in Faucigny and Gex. 'recognition as the undisputed sovereign of Faucigny and the county of Gex'. Cliopatria's Dauphiné row ends in 1351. [Reviewer eu-13-h, 2026-10-25: counterpart changed from dauphine (its dossier ends in 1351) to kingdom-of-france: the Amadeus VI page has Humbert II surrender 'his title and principality to the future King Charles V of France' in 1349.]

region.text: Savoyard lands in Dauphiné beyond the Rhone and the Guiers

ledger.note: 1355: Savoy gives up its lands in Dauphiné. 'Amadeus agreed to exchange territory in Dauphiné beyond the rivers Rhone and Guiers'. The pages do not say where these lands lay, and Cliopatria's Savoy shape holds none of them (Isère cells appear only from 1402, on the Savoy side of the Guiers); the Isère side of the Rhône (a 15 km band) stands for them. [Reviewer eu-13-h, 2026-10-25: counterpart changed from dauphine (its dossier ends in 1351) to kingdom-of-france: the Amadeus VI page has Humbert II surrender 'his title and principality to the future King Charles V of France' in 1349.]

28 September 1388: Nice and the Ubaye valley. 'Nice became part of the domains of the House of Savoy on 28 September 1388', negotiated by Amadeus VII with Giovanni Grimaldi 'taking advantage of the internal struggles in Provence'; the Ubaye valley passes at the same time. Amadeus VII's page: 'In 1388, he acquired territories in eastern Provence and the port city of Nice'. Cliopatria's Provence-side neighbour is the dossier county-of-provence, whose ledger has the matching loss.

region.text: the Piedmont cells of Cliopatria's 1395 shape (Turin, Cuneo, Vercelli, Biella, Novara)

ledger.note: Piedmont cells appear in Cliopatria's 1395 shape (Turin province 13, Cuneo 5, Biella 4, Vercelli 2, Novara 1). Neither Amadeus VII's nor Amadeus VI's page mentions any acquisition in Piedmont; the year is Cliopatria's. Page silent.

region.text: the County of Geneva, largely the later Genevois province

ledger.note: 1401: Savoy buys the County of Geneva. 'In 1401, Odo sold the County to' Amadeus VIII; infobox 'Purchased by Savoy: 1401'. The page adds that 'From 1424 the County of Geneva was joined to the House of Savoy' (the legal process). The county was 'largely corresponding to the later Genevois province', with its capital at Annecy from 1219; Cliopatria's 1402 shape shows the purchase only as the two cells of the canton of Geneva, the Annecy country being inside the Savoy shape from 1260.

region.text: 12 cells of Cliopatria's 1402 shape that no page explains

ledger.note: Cliopatria's 1402 shape adds 12 cells (Isère 4, Vercelli 2, Savoie 2, Haute-Savoie 2, Turin 1, Biella 1) that none of the pages opened explains. Page silent.

1416: Savoy becomes a duchy. 'The duchy was created in 1416 when Sigismund, Holy Roman Emperor... awarded the title of "Duke" to Count Amadeus VIII.' The Duchy page adds the Principality of Piedmont 'in August 1424'.

region.text: one cell on the south shore of Lake Neuchâtel (6.76 E, 46.81 N)

ledger.note: Cliopatria's shape loses one cell on the south shore of Lake Neuchâtel in 1475. The Duchy page: 'As a consequence of its participation in the Burgundian Wars, Savoy lost all its possessions north and south-east of Lake Geneva to the Swiss' (no year; and Vaud stays Savoyard in the shape and, per the Canton page, to 1536). Page silent on the year.

1536: Bern annexes Vaud. 'As the power of the House of Savoy declined at the beginning of the 15th century, troops from Bern occupied the land'; 'By 1536 Bern had completely annexed the area.' The Duchy page gives no mention of Vaud's loss.

region.text: the duchy occupied by France, without Vaud

ledger.note: 1536: France occupies the duchy. 'Ultimately in 1536, Francis ordered the occupation of the duchy, which was invaded by a strong military contingent'; Turin 'was lost on 3 April of the same year' (the Italian War page: Chabot 'led his army into Piedmont in March 1536, and proceeded to capture Turin the following month'). Infobox 'Occupied by France: 1536-59'; 'Charles III retreated to Vercelli, trying to continue the fight'.

region.text: the duchy occupied by France, without Vaud

ledger.note: 1559: the occupation ends. 'The Peace of Cateau-Cambrésis, signed in 1559, restored full autonomy to the duchy'; Emmanuel Philibert managed 'to put an end to the more than twenty-year long occupation'. Infobox 'Occupied by France: 1536-59'.

region.text: the Duchy of Savoy as restored in 1559, less Vaud

ledger.note: 1559: the occupied duchy is restored and passes to the House of Savoy dossier. This is a hand-over inside one state, not a dissolution: the Duchy page has the duchy from 1416 to 1720 and moving its capital to Turin in 1562 ('He therefore moved the capital from Chambéry to Turin in 1562'). Keep one colour.

wars.name: Savoyard war for Faucigny and Gex
wars.outcome: Savoy took Gex in the siege of 26 October to 11 November 1353 and was 'recognised as the undisputed sovereign of Faucigny and the county of Gex' by the Treaty of Paris of 1355, giving up its lands in Dauphiné beyond the Rhone and Guiers.
wars.note: The page names 'Hugh's forces' at Gex in 1353 but not the Dauphin; the war's name is the researcher's.

wars.name: Savoyard sieges of Geneva
wars.outcome: 'Charles launched a surprise attack in July 1534, but his army was beaten back'; 'A second siege in October 1535 was attempted, and again Charles's army was defeated.' No change of border: the city of Geneva was not Savoyard land in the shape.

wars.name: Bernese annexation of Vaud
wars.outcome: 'By 1536 Bern had completely annexed the area.'
wars.note: The Duchy page puts the loss 'as a consequence of its participation in the Burgundian Wars', without dates; the Canton page puts the end in 1536. The month is not on either page.

wars.name: Italian War of 1536-1538
wars.outcome: France invaded the duchy in 1536 ('Francis ordered the occupation of the duchy'); the Truce of Nice of 18 June 1538 'ended the war, leaving Turin in French hands'; the occupation lasted to 1559.
wars.note: The page contradicts itself on Piedmont: the Truce section says Charles 'had to abandon his to give Piedmont back to the House of Savoy', while the infobox and lead say 'Savoy and Piedmont acquired by France'. No Savoyard land is drawn as restored in 1538.

certainty.note: The lordships of the Alps and the Rhône are approximate; Savoy's limits moved with marriages and sales, not surveyed lines.

The Treaty of Paris of 1355 settled the Dauphiné frontier on 'the rivers Rhone and Guiers'; the county of Nice lay 'between the Mediterranean Sea, Var River and the southernmost crest of the Alps'. The Piedmont cells (1395) and the Alpine crest towards the Valais are soft.
The lands under French occupation and the exiled duke's remnant are known only as 'most of his lands'.

notes: The County of Savoy is Cliopatria's row 1260-1539; the pages make it the same state as the Duchy of Savoy (1416 onward), which the house-of-savoy dossier carries from 1559 (it names county-of-savoy as its predecessor). This dossier therefore runs 1003 to 1559: it adds the 257 years Cliopatria lacks before 1260 (new keyframes _1003, _1046, _1218) and the French occupation after 1539 (_1536). The dissolve event of 1559 is a hand-over, not an end; keep one colour. Method for the blocks: the pages date what Savoy gained (Vaud 1218, Bresse 1272, Faucigny and Gex 1355, Nice 1388, Geneva 1401) but Cliopatria shows all of Vaud, Bresse, Faucigny, Gex and Geneva only in its 1402 shape (and Nice with Piedmont in 1395); each block is written as Cliopatria's own 1402 cells within a named department, canton or disc, so the sum of the blocks is exactly Cliopatria's 1402 shape. 12 cells of that shape (Isère 4, Vercelli 2, Savoie 2, Haute-Savoie 2, Turin 1, Biella 1) and the 25 Piedmont cells of 1395 are explained by no page opened (confidence 1 events). Pages disagree or are silent: the Canton of Vaud page puts the counts of Savoy in Vaud from 1218 and Bern's annexation by 1536, while the Duchy page says Savoy lost 'all its possessions north and south-east of Lake Geneva to the Swiss' as a consequence of the Burgundian Wars (undated), and Cliopatria keeps Vaud to 1539 (a 1475 cell loss only); the Italian War page says both that Piedmont went back to Savoy and that France acquired it; the County of Savoy page dates Imperial immediacy 1313 in the text and 1331 in the infobox; the Amadeus VI page gives his death as 27 February and 1 March 1383. Not on the pages opened (so not drawn): Peter II's and Philip I's acquisitions in the 1260s-1280s, Amadeus V's Imperial immediacy, Bugey, the Principality of Achaea and Piedmont (1418), Vercelli (1427), the Burgundian Wars' territorial effect, Geneva's and Chablais's loss in 1536 (Valais, Bern), the Truce of Nice, the exiled duke's remnant, and the Treaty of Lausanne (1564). Suzerainty (not territory): Charles IV 'transferred the County of Savoy from the Kingdom of Burgundy to the Kingdom of Germany' in 1361 and made Amadeus VI Imperial vicar of Arelat in 1365 (the Cliopatria umbrella '(Holy Roman Empire)' lists Savoy 1260-1458); the Kingdom of Arles dossier already carries the 1361 event. No ruler strip: the pages opened give only fragments of the regnal list (Peter II 1263-68, Philip I 1268-85, Amadeus VI 1343-83, Amadeus VII 1383-91, Charles III 1504-53). No capital is named for 1003-1294. No infobox area on any page opened, so the area comparison could not be made; Cliopatria's 14,987 to 35,962 km2 are unchecked. Counterparts without a dossier: March of Turin, County of Geneva (needs a dossier, suggested slug county-of-geneva), Bishops of Aosta. Gazetteer names missing: Maurienne, Tarentaise, Chablais, Faucigny, Genevois, Bresse, Bugey, Gex, Viennois (a disc and department stand in for each).
